\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2015 SCORING GUIDELINES}

\section*{Question 5}

The figure above shows the graph of \(f^{\prime}\), the derivative of a twice-differentiable function \(f\), on the interval [-3, 4]. The graph of \(f^{\prime}\) has horizontal tangents at \(x=-1, x=1\), and \(x=3\). The areas of the regions bounded by the \(x\)-axis and the graph of \(f^{\prime}\) on the intervals [-2, 1] and [1, 4] are 9 and 12 , respectively.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find all \(x\)-coordinates at which \(f\) has a relative maximum. Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(b)] On what open intervals contained in \(-3<x<4\) is the graph of \(f\) both concave down and decreasing? Give a reason for your answer.
\end{itemize}
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/be09582e-415b-462a-861c-4218626861a9-1.jpg?height=505&width=776&top_left_y=400&top_left_x=1156)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(c)] Find the \(x\)-coordinates of all points of inflection for the graph of \(f\). Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(d)] Given that \(f(1)=3\), write an expression for \(f(x)\) that involves an integral. Find \(f(4)\) and \(f(-2)\).
\item[(a)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=0\) at \(x=-2, x=1\), and \(x=4\).
\(f^{\prime}(x)\) changes from positive to negative at \(x=-2\).
Therefore, \(f\) has a relative maximum at \(x=-2\).
\item[(b)] The graph of \(f\) is concave down and decreasing on the intervals \(-2<x<-1\) and \(1<x<3\) because \(f^{\prime}\) is decreasing and negative on these intervals.
\item[(c)] The graph of \(f\) has a point of inflection at \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\) because \(f^{\prime}\) changes from decreasing to increasing at these points.
The graph of \(f\) has a point of inflection at \(x=1\) because \(f^{\prime}\) changes from increasing to decreasing at this point.
\item[(d)] \(f(x)=3+\int_{1}^{x} f^{\prime}(t) d t\)
\[
f(4)=3+\int_{1}^{4} f^{\prime}(t) d t=3+(-12)=-9
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(-2) & =3+\int_{1}^{-2} f^{\prime}(t) d t=3-\int_{-2}^{1} f^{\prime}(t) d t \\
& =3-(-9)=12
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { identifies } x=-2 \\ 1: \text { answer with reason }\end{array}\right.\)
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { intervals } \\ 1: \text { reason }\end{array}\right.\)
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { identifies } x=-1,1, \text { and } 3 \\ 1: \text { reason }\end{array}\right.\)
\(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { expression for } f(x) \\ 1: f(4) \text { and } f(-2)\end{array}\right.\)
